summary: An open-source coding-font site by Belleve Invis, styled like a dark IDE: everything is set in Iosevka with cyan used only for emphasis, and each chapter pairs a large thin title with a short note and a working sampler. Its depth is in the live feature pickers: 19 stylistic sets, 63 cherry-pickable characters and 21 ligation sets, with the results handed to a customizer.

instances.feel: Precise, cold, like a boot screen
instances.ux: Download goes to GitHub releases, Customize to a build page. Version number is shown first, as for software
instances.learn: Showing the current version beside the download treats the typeface as living software, which is what its audience expects

instances.look: 'Variants à la Carte': a style toolbar and a dimmed live character sample, then 'Stylistic Sets' (ss01–ss20 named after famous code fonts: Andale Mono Style, Consolas Style, Menlo Style…) and a 'Cherry-Picking' grid of 63 characters each with a dropdown caret
instances.feel: Like a settings panel for a font
instances.ux: Pick a set or open a character's dropdown to choose its variant, and the sample above updates. Each option has a tooltip with its CSS (cv01 2) and TOML config; right click resets. 'Show Usage' and 'Bake Custom Build' side tiles export the choice
instances.learn: Naming stylistic sets after the fonts people already love ('Menlo Style') makes alternates instantly understandable; cherry-picking per glyph with CSS and TOML in the tooltip turns the specimen into a configuration tool

instances.look: 'Coding Ligations': a board of ligature sequences (arrows, comparison, comment markers) where sequences not enabled in the active set stay dim, above a grid of set switches tagged with OpenType tags (calt, dlig, CLIK, JSPT, PHPX, HSKL, MTLB…), each named for a language
instances.ux: Clicking a language switch relights the board, so a Haskell or C user sees exactly which ligatures apply; a toolbar also changes style, weight, slope and width
instances.learn: A single board with dim and lit states shows both what a ligature set does and what it leaves out, which a list of pairs can't
